subject: Civil Engineering
title: Hydropower Generation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Hydropower Generation.

hook.text: Water falls through a turbine — spinning magnets past coils — and electricity flows out.

buildup.text: Power depends on head (height of fall) and flow (volume of water) — more of either means more watts.

discovery.text: Penstocks — large steel pipes — channel water from the reservoir to the turbines below.

twist.text: Pumped-storage plants pump water back uphill at night — then generate when demand peaks.

climax.text: The Three Gorges Dam generates 22,500 MW — enough to power 20 million homes.

punchline.text: Falling water spins a turbine. Gravity does the work — clean power, endlessly renewed.

quiz.question: What two factors determine how much power a hydroelectric dam generates?
options: Head (height of water fall) and flow (volume of water through turbines)
Reservoir surface area and water temperature
